title: GPU round 9: which change ships
question:
Which GPU change, if any, should ship, and what is the next build?
Candidates: every GPU change that has an interleaved A/B against default in the data — compact state (POGO_GPU_STUDY=stack), occupancy (occni), tail speculation (tail), tail with certain feed (tail,certain) and tail v2. Decide by warm seconds per generation in the interleaved A/B (10-gen halving-3 standard command): a change ships when its gain beats both arms' spreads with at least 2 runs per arm, and its results are identical to default (verify 100%, same-seed checkpoints identical). Also report, for the change that ships, its tail share against default and the full standard run's total wall against default.

problem.quote: I thought number 4 was one of the things I originally requested—I.e, removing unneeded wait times. I want it
problem.quote_from: you, in the planner session (round 9 Ask)
problem.why: Each warm generation ends with GPU lanes idle while the last battles finish, and every standard run pays for that wait.

first.verdict: Compact state ships.[[ship]] It is faster than default in every pair and its results match.
first.next_action: Diff its checkpoints against default's, then time one full run of each.
first.deciding: Compact state {w_stack_mean|bare} vs default {w_base_mean|bare} per warm gen, n = {w_stack_n|bare} vs {w_base_n|bare}, spreads {w_stack_spread|bare} vs {w_base_spread|bare} ({w_stack_mean|src}).[[pairs]]
wrong_or_missing: Nobody finished a full standard run, so it's not measured.
Full-tail-1 crashed at gen {ft_gens|bare} of {ft_planned|bare}, so it's not run.
Files disagree on a tail share, {ts_r9def_runsall|bare} vs {ts_r9def_lit|bare} (conflict, evidence-profile).
Tail v2 ran once, so it's unproven.

sections.heading: Compact state against default, pair by pair

blocks.p: Compact state (POGO_GPU_STUDY=stack) keeps each battle's state in smaller 8- and 16-bit fields, so the struct shrinks.
The morning A/B alternated default, compact state and occupancy for three rounds on the same GPU (ab.log, every run exited clean).
Compact state wins every round. Its mean gain of {stack_diff|bare} ({stack_pct|bare}) is larger than its spread of {w_stack_spread|bare} and default's {w_base_spread|bare}.
Its results match default. verify_3v3 winner agreement is {verify_stack|bare} with {verify_stack_flagged|bare} flagged rows ({verify_stack|src}).
stack/result.json says the overnight chain's checkpoints equal base-a, a default run, citing a determinism.txt outside this data.
In the morning logs, every generation's fitness line and the final top team match between ab-stack-1..3 and ab-base-1..3.
Logs are not checkpoints, so the diff still comes first.
The 10-gen total wall moved with it, {tot_stack_mean|bare} against {tot_base_mean|bare}, a difference of {tot_diff|bare} (runs-all.json total).

sections.heading: Compact state's tail share, and the full run nobody finished

blocks.p: Tail share is the scorer's tailShare field in runs-all.json, the warm generations' tail bucket divided by their wall (gpu-profile.json).
Compact state's tail share is {ts_stack_mean|bare} against default's {ts_base_mean|bare}. The {ts_diff|bare} point gap is inside both spreads ({ts_stack_spread|bare} and {ts_base_spread|bare}).
So the tail is as large as before. Compact state speeds up the whole launch, and the tail with it.
The full standard run's total wall is not measured for either arm. runs.json lists every full run as null.
No full run of compact state exists. The only full run of the standard recipe, full-tail-1, exited {ft_exit|bare} at gen {ft_gens|bare} of {ft_planned|bare}.
The sidecar lost the GPU lock, so it is not run and its wall is not a figure.
Two older 100-gen full runs also failed, r9pre-full-tail at gen {fulltail_pre_gens|bare} and r9pre-full-certain at gen {fullcert_pre_gens|bare}, so they are not run either.
Occupancy (POGO_GPU_STUDY=occ POGO_GPU_OCC=ni) compiles the kernel's cold helpers as real function calls.
Its mean gain of {occni_diff|bare} is inside its own spread of {w_occni_spread|bare}, because round two ran slow. The verdict is unproven.
The occ fork's overnight chain put occupancy at {occ_ni_mean|bare} (n = {occ_ni_n|bare}) against production's {occ_prod_mean|bare} (n = {occ_prod_n|bare}) (runs-all.json).
occ/runs.json averages all nine warm gens instead and gives slightly different means.
Production there is the stock kernel on the same code with no interleaving plan, so this chain is listed under Also measured.

sections.heading: Tail speculation and the certain feed in the 11:53 ET A/B

blocks.p: Tail speculation (POGO_GPU_STUDY=tail) lets idle GPU lanes run next-round battles while a launch's last battles finish.
The certain feed (tail,certain) adds the battles of teams already sure to survive the cut.
The 11:53 ET A/B alternated default, tail and tail with certain feed for three rounds (the r9pre runs).

chart.title: Warm s/gen, 11:53 ET A/B (r9pre runs)
chart.axis_reason: The bars differ by about a second on a 13-second scale. From zero they look alike.
chart.reading: Default is ahead. Tail is {tail_diff|bare} slower and the certain feed {cert_diff|bare} slower, and both gaps clear every spread.

blocks.p: Both give default's answers. verify_3v3 winner agreement is {verify_tail|bare} for tail and {verify_cert|bare} for the certain feed, {verify_tail_flagged|bare} flagged.
det-r9.txt shows {det_tail_ckpts|bare} same-seed checkpoints identical to default for tail and {det_cert_ckpts|bare} for the certain feed.
The verdict is rerun because the one later run went the other way. In the afternoon A/B tail took {w_r9tail_runsall|bare} against default's {w_r9def_runsall|bare}.
That is one run each, because r9-ab-default-2 stopped at gen {r9def2_gens|bare} with no exit code.
At n = {w_r9_n|bare} the gain is unproven, so the later build needs its own A/B.

sections.heading: The afternoon A/B and what runs.json got wrong

blocks.p: The afternoon r9 runs at 14:05 ET are a later build of the same flags. Two files describe them and disagree.
runs.json stores the 11:53 values under the afternoon names.
Its certain entry has {r9cert_gens_runsjson|bare} generations and a null exit, and it started at 11:58 ET.
The afternoon certain run finished with exit {r9cert_exit_runsall|bare} after {r9cert_gens_runsall|bare} gens (runs-all.json). One run beside one default, so unproven.
The tail share conflict is the same mislabel. runs.json's {ts_r9def_runsjson|bare} is the 11:53 run's value.
The afternoon run's own profile gives {ts_r9def_runsall|bare}.
evidence-profile measures the share of the launch span instead, and gives a third warm figure for this run, {w_r9def_lit|bare}.
Tail v2 (POGO_GPU_STUDY=tail,v2) lowers the speculation threshold from half the workers idle to a quarter.
One run, no interleaved default and no spread, so there is no gain to report and the row is unproven.
A three-round A/B against default on the fixed code would settle it.

also_measured: Compact state's overnight chain, {chain_stack_warm} over n = {chain_stack_n|bare} runs vs production's {chain_prod_warm} over n = {chain_prod_n|bare} ({chain_stack_warm|src}).
A {full100_default_gens|bare}-gen default-only run, r9-full-default, took {full100_default_total} in total. Longer than the standard recipe, no partner arm.
runs.json's A/B block holds the 11:53 ET values under afternoon names, default {w_r9def_runsjson} and tail {w_r9tail_runsjson}.
checked: the compact-state checkpoint diff against default, which no file in the data holds

evidence.claim: Compact state is the one change whose gain clears both spreads.
Compact state is faster in all three pairs of the morning A/B.

evidence.note: Only the logs were compared. The checkpoint diff cites a determinism log that is not in the data.

evidence.claim: Tail and tail plus certain were slower than default in the 11:53 ET A/B.
Nobody finished a full standard run.
Two files disagree on r9-ab-default-1's tail share. Both values are in the Wrong-or-missing box.
evidence.note: The other side is lit/evidence-profile.json, field tail_share.

evidence.claim: Tail v2 ran once, with no default run beside it.
The afternoon A/B lost a default run, and runs.json stores the 11:53 ET values under the afternoon names.
